A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAIN research. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable. The missing result tables in v2 are document omissions rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original TriviaQA and TruthfulQA attack results, commercial-model evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original QA experiments and adds a scientific peer-review experiment and concrete examples of optimized prompts and model responses.

M1.justification: The AAP initialization followed by greedy word perturbation, attack losses, word-importance calculation and stopping logic remain intact. Expanded templates and explanations do not establish a procedural revision; the stated helper-model substitution is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: V2 retains TriviaQA and the same six TruthfulQA categories. Section 7 adds a limited experiment using accepted and rejected ICLR 2025 papers, extending evaluation to scientific peer-review decisions and longer document inputs.

E2.justification: V1 Table A4 reports Llama2-7B targeted comparisons with NSP, Manual, M+Greedy and AAP. V2 omits that table, retaining only selected AAP/CAIN aggregates in prose and losing the other comparator results for this experiment. The new Table 1 categorizes existing attacks without empirically evaluating them.

E3.justification: Sections 3–4 change the stated paraphrasing and Stage-1 evaluation model from GPT-4o to GPT-4o-mini, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. The new peer-review protocol uses six benign papers, one target paper, and twenty separate evaluation papers, reporting accuracy with GPT-4o-mini.

E4.justification: V2 adds the peer-review case study and two AAP-versus-CAIN response examples in Tables A9–A10. Existing threshold, benign-set-size, model-size and perplexity analyses survive, including the full model-size plot relocated to Figure A3. Detailed Llama2 targeted format-transfer and initialization comparisons are omitted.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports seed 42 for benign-example sampling. Existing shaded plots and perplexity boxplots remain, with no newly specified repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Matched main QA tables and retained initialization results are numerically unchanged. V2 adds roughly 40% peer-review accuracy for both handcrafted and optimized prompts, plus two response examples. Most Llama2 targeted entries and the full GPT-4.1-nano comparison disappear, although selected values survive in prose.

T1.justification: The attack objectives, semantic-similarity constraint, prompt score and word-importance formula retain the same mathematical content. Equation renumbering and notation changes are cosmetic. The new geometric comparison with jailbreaking is conceptual and introduces no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim selective manipulation through human-readable, black-box system-prompt optimization while preserving benign behavior. The three principal contributions and headline claims of up to 40% untargeted F1 degradation and over 70% targeted F1 remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 tentatively attributes benign degradation to limited benign samples. V2 develops an inherent-trade-off explanation involving semantic overlap, target specificity and the constraints supplied by benign examples. It also interprets the peer-review outcome as a difficulty with biased models and adds explicit limitations concerning long inputs, models above 32B and non-English evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 supplies actual evaluator, analyzer and generator prompts and a stepwise AAP description. It newly documents GPU hardware, 8-bit quantization, correctness thresholds and SentenceTransformer-based answer mapping. A code link replaces v1's promise of future release. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to previously undisclosed settings.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against jailbreaking through Figure 2 and Table 1, emphasizing optimization direction, benign preservation and black-box access. It adds JailbreakEdit and Sentence-BERT citations and removes the Ayers, Bender and Weidinger references. Most previously discussed attack literature remains.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites and expands the introduction, condenses numbered method and experiment subsections, creates a separate commercial-chatbot section, and combines limitations with the conclusion. It removes the standalone ethics statement, shortens the title and adds substantial appendix explanations.

P2.justification: V2 redraws introductory and framework diagrams, adds a conceptual comparison figure and feature table, and introduces prompt/example tables and a propagation diagram. Existing plots are relocated or partially redisplayed, and initialization results are split across tables. Table 3 adds grouping headers but misleadingly labels the retained aggregate scores as 'Difference'.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the method easier to inspect through actual prompts, implementation and scoring details, a code pointer, and concrete examples. The peer-review probe and expanded limitations also clarify applicability. These provide a limited overall gain, tempered by missing Llama2 and GPT-4.1-nano comparisons, unresolved appendix references and the misleading aggregate-column label. The central QA evidence is unchanged.
